newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank sees no severe price risks-Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank sees no severe price risks-Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Monday the German central bank sees no grave risks for price developments despite the dollar's recent surge against the mark and slightly stronger German inflation.
Gaddum told Germany's Handelsblatt daily newspaper that the Bundesbank saw "no price dangers that could have a severe impact on us."
An advance summary of the interview to be published on Tuesday was made available in advance. It was not clear exactly when the comments were made.
The newspaper also quoted Gaddum as saying there was no reason to talk the dollar up or down from its present level.

On money supply, the Bundesbank's prime policy indicator, Gaddum said the supply had risen by an annualised 5.9 percent in the last six months of 1996 "so we were comfortably within our target range."
The Bundesbank was aiming for money supply growth of four to seven percent in 1996.
